title: POC: workload topology & latency gating - StellaMart POC scoping
next_steps: Jordan to send benchmark spreadsheet and synthetic traffic generator repo by 2028-02-09
Priya to propose three model/quantization options and cost estimates by 2028-02-10
Customer to share 7-day traffic histogram and recent promotion calendar by 2028-02-11
Schedule in-region bench run at StellaMart staging environment week of 2028-02-13
action_items: Carlos/Mei: export 7-day qps/concurrency telemetry and example prompts (due 2028-02-11)
Omar: open firewall for Redwood bench runner IPs and confirm VPC peering window (due 2028-02-12)
summary: Discovery-style scoping to pin down workload topology for a StellaMart POC. Primary goals: define QPS/concurrency profiles (steady, promotional bursts), measure token length distribution (input prompts vs generated responses), set latency SLOs and cost targets, and agree bench plan and timeline. AE + SE present from Redwood; customer provided infra and product context. Agreed next steps and owners.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hi everyone — thanks for hopping on. We're on for 50 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Carlos: Carlos here — head of ML.
[00:08] Mei: Mei Chen, platform.
[00:10] Diane: Diane Park, product.
[00:12] Omar: Omar Haddad, SRE.
[00:14] Priya (SE): Priya Natarajan, Redwood SE. Hi all.
[00:18] Jordan: Great. The goal today is to scope the POC: what success looks like, what traffic shapes we need to emulate, and how we'll run benchmarks. Priya will sketch the bench plan.
[02:05] Priya: Quick note on approach: we usually collect a 7-day telemetry dump if possible, then build a synthetic replay that captures diurnal patterns, poisson-ish arrivals plus heavier promotional bursts. For retail, bursts matter — flash sales cause 5-10x QPS spikes for 10-30 minutes.
[02:30] Carlos: Yeah our Black Friday-like promos give us spikes up to around 420 QPS from a baseline of ~45 QPS. But that was an anomaly window; typical peak weekday is 120-150 QPS.
[03:00] Diane: To add context, the LLM is powering product Q&A and assisted search snippets. When we fall back to cached answers latency needs to be under 200ms but for generative pieces product expects ~1s to 2s at the top end.
[03:24] Jordan: Good — that helps. Can you confirm concurrency? How many simultaneous sessions are open during peaks?
[03:40] Mei: We measure concurrency differently — our front end opens long-poll-ish websockets. During high peaks concurrent active prompts ~220, but model-level concurrency (in flight tokens) closer to 40-60 depending on prompt lengths.
[04:10] Priya: That difference is important. For sizing we care about in-flight model concurrency and token throughput (tokens/sec) more than socket counts.
[04:30] Omar: Our average prompt size is small — around 30-60 input tokens — but responses vary a lot; mean output around 140 tokens, median 100, heavy tail to 800+ for long explanations.
[05:10] Priya: That token heavy tail changes memory/KV cache needs and latency. We'll want to capture the distribution: 60% of responses under 120 tokens, 30% 120--300, 10% >300.
[05:35] Jordan: What are your latency goals for the POC? We typically gate on p95 and p99 for end-to-end response.
[05:48] Diane: Product wants p95 end-to-end under 800ms for the 150-token class. p99 under 2.5s is acceptable during bursts but we'd like graceful degradation.
[06:10] Priya: So we should set bench targets: p95 < 800ms at baseline traffic (45 QPS), and p95 < 1.2s up to steady peak (150 QPS). Then test burst condition at 400 QPS where we allow fallbacks and measure cost.
[06:35] Jordan: Cost target? Any ballpark per-user or per-invocation cost you need us to hit?
[06:42] Carlos: We want to keep inference cost below $0.0008 per generated token on average. If Redwood can demonstrate under $0.0006 with quantized model variants that would be great.
[07:05] Priya: We'll include multiple model profiles: A) medium-latency high-quality (base 3B quantized 4-bit), B) balanced (7B int8), C) higher-throughput 13B-quantized with lower quality. We'll map them to cost/latency curves.
[07:30] Mei: We run in us-west-2 for staging; will want a bench run in that region. Network hops add ~30-40ms typically.
[08:00] Jordan: Good. On telemetry, what fields can you export? We need timestamped request logs with input token count, output token count, response time, model id (if available), and request path.
[08:18] Carlos: We can export logs but model id is not recorded at the moment; we can add a tag for the POC.
[08:28] Diane: Also share the promotion calendar — the dates where you expect bursts so Redwood can schedule bench runs that are meaningful.
[08:40] Priya: For benchmark design we'll do three phases: 1) footprint and cold-start: measure model boot times, kv cache priming; 2) steady-state replay: run 7-day histogram compressed into a 4-hour run to validate p95/p99 at baseline and steady peak; 3) burst stress: synthetic oversubscription to simulate promo spikes and validate fallback policies.
[09:15] Omar: Curious about KV caching — during product Q&A we have repeated patterns that could be cached. How does Redwood handle prefix caching?
[09:30] Priya: Redwood has prefix/KV cache options; in Dedicated or Private you can tune cache TTL and warm-up strategy. For POC we'll test two cache configs: conservative TTL (per request) and aggressive TTL (5 min) and report hit rates.
[09:55] Jordan: Let's talk observability — what metrics do you want from us?
[10:02] Mei: We need token-level cost breakdown, p50/p95/p99 latency, per-model throughput, error rates and retries, and traces for slow requests.
[10:15] Priya: We'll provide dashboards and a raw CSV for the bench so you can run your own analysis.
[10:24] Carlos: For success criteria: 1) p95 latency under 800ms at baseline, 2) p95 under 1.2s at steady peak, 3) graceful degradation during bursts (failover to smaller model or cached responses), 4) cost under $0.0008/token average across week.
[11:00] Jordan: Sounds good. Any regulatory or compliance asks for Private deployment?
[11:06] Diane: We're not in scope for PII redaction but need audit logs and SSO via SAML. If Private, we need KMS integration for keys.
[11:20] Priya: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM and we have SOC2 docs; Jordan will include the security one-pager.
[11:30] Omar: Regarding network, we might prefer VPC peering for bench runs — less noisy neighbors.
[11:36] Jordan: OK we'll add network options to the run plan.
[11:45] Priya: For the synthetic generator we'll give you a script that replays variable token-length responses with configurable shape: log-normal for token lengths and poisson for arrivals with tunable burst windows.
[12:00] Carlos: Will the replay include user-level correlation? Some users fire multiple sequential prompts (a short follow-up), that impacts KV reuse and latency patterns.
[12:12] Priya: Good catch. We'll include session affinity in the replay to model follow-ups and cache hits: roughly 25% of requests are follow-ups within 30s in your data.
[12:30] Mei: Our infra note: we run behind a homegrown gateway that does rate-limiting at 1k RPS and then fanout to LLM stack. We'll need to consider rate-limiter interplay.
[13:00] Jordan: We'll test bench both with and without your gateway to capture realistic queuing effects.
[13:20] Diane: Timeline? When can you deliver the bench plan and the initial run?
[13:30] Jordan: We can send the benchmark spreadsheet and replay scripts by 2028-02-09. If you can share telemetry by 2028-02-11, we can prep a staging run and schedule the in-region bench the week of 2028-02-13. Expect initial results within 72 hours of the run.
[14:00] Priya: For measurements we'll collect token throughput (tokens/sec), model-level concurrency, per-request latency buckets, and cost per token. We'll also do a variance analysis for tail latency contributors: model compute vs scheduling vs network.
[15:10] Omar: On security checklist — can you share required ports and IP ranges?
[15:18] Jordan: Yes, will attach network requirements and the redwood bench runner IP list.
[15:30] Carlos: Any gotchas with quantization? We worry about hallucination regressions with aggressive quant.
[15:40] Priya: We'll include quality regression checks vs your eval set — automatic BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics plus spot human checks for hallucination. That's part of the model profile comparison.
[16:05] Diane: Who's our main contact for day-to-day?
[16:10] Jordan: Jordan and Priya — Jordan for contract/pricing, Priya for bench and technical. Liam will be on-call for bench run days.
[16:30] Priya: Quick note: we'll instrument a lightweight agent to sample KV sizes and memory during the runs to recommend instance types.
[16:45] Mei: For dedicated capacity, we'd need a cost estimate and a recommended minimum GPU footprint for steady 150 QPS.
[16:55] Priya: We'll provide a throughput map: expected QPS per GPU for each model profile and target latency — that should make capacity planning straightforward.
[17:15] Jordan: Ok let's do a short recap of next steps.
[17:22] Carlos: Recap please.
[17:24] Jordan: 1) Jordan: send benchmark sheet/replay script by 2/9. 2) Priya: model options + cost by 2/10. 3) StellaMart (Carlos/Mei): telemetry + promotion calendar by 2/11. 4) Omar: open firewall/VPC peering window by 2/12. 5) Schedule bench week of 2/13.
[17:50] Diane: That works. Also please include the security one-pager and SOC2 artifact.
[18:02] Jordan: Will do. Anything else?
[18:10] Carlos: No, good meeting.
[18:12] Mei: Thanks everyone.
[18:14] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up in email with links. End call.
[50:45] [recording stops]
